articles.description:
Protecting a document is not the same as proving it exists


When people talk about “protecting” a document, they usually mean one thing:
Encryption, passwords, access control, secure storage — all of these are about confidentiality.
But there is another dimension that is often overlooked.
You can encrypt a file perfectly and still be unable to prove that it existed at a specific point in time.
If someone challenges your authorship, your idea, or your work, encryption alone does not help.
you have something, not when it existed.
This is where a different kind of protection appears.
Protecting existence means being able to prove that a document existed at a given moment — without revealing its content.
This is done by computing a cryptographic fingerprint (hash) of the file and anchoring th…
articles.title: Protecting a document is not the same as proving it exists

articles.description:
Cloud computing has quietly become the backbone of modern technology. From streaming movies to running business apps, it allows users to access data and services over the internet instead of relying on physical hardware.
One of the biggest advantages of cloud computing is scalability. Businesses can increase or decrease resources based on demand, paying only for what they use. This makes it cost-effective and ideal for startups as well as large enterprises.
Cloud platforms also improve accessibility and collaboration. Teams can work on the same data in real time from different locations, boosting productivity and flexibility.
In short, cloud computing removes the limits of traditional IT infrastructure and enables faster innovation. As technology evolves, the cloud will continue to shape how we build, store, and share digital experiences.
articles.title: Cloud Computing: Powering the Digital World from Anywhere

articles.author: Michael Amachree
articles.description:
It’s Day 8 of 12 Days of Svelte Apps 🎄
Holiday cooking is fun… right up until the recipe switches units on you.
cups vs milliliters
ounces vs grams
Fahrenheit vs Celsius
So today’s mini-app is the Unit Converter — a clean, fast converter you can keep open while you cook.
🔗 Try it live: https://svelte-apps.me/apps/unit-converter
💻 View the code: https://github.com/Michael-Obele/Svelte-MiniApps/tree/main/src/routes/apps/(app)/unit-converter
The UI is intentionally simple:
Pick a unit category (Volume, Temperature, Mass, etc.)
Enter a value
Choose “From” and “To” units
Get a formatted result instantly
It also includes a Swap button so you can flip the direction quickly, and a Clear action to reset the input.
Results are formatted cleanly (so you don’t get unreadable long decimals)
It handles "same unit" conversions gracefully
It supports a wide set of categories beyond cooking too (length, area, time, angle, data, energy, force, power, pressure)
If your recipe says 350°F but you’re using a °C oven, pick Temperature and convert.
For recipes written in US cups, pick Volume and convert to mL for a measuring jug.
For baking (where precision matters), converting to grams can make measuring a lot easier.
If you try it, post a conversion you used today (or a recipe you’re making) and tag me.
articles.title: Day 8: Recipe Conversions Without the Panic (Unit Converter)
